newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call inactive, security prices firm up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call inactive, security prices firm up.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities firmed up in brisk trade while the call money market was inactive on the reporting Friday, dealers said.
Banks do not normally borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.

"There were only quotes for overnight money today," said a dealer. "Three-day money was traded between 4.5 and 5.5 percent, indicating that call money will open around seven to eight percent tomorrow."
Dealers said prices of government securities were steady to firm in brisk trade.
The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Friday at 99.12 rupees against its last traded 99.0 rupees while the 12.50 precent 2004 was traded at 95.90 rupees against 99.55, they said.
The 13.40 percent 1999 stock was little changed at 100.85 against 100.84, dealers said.
Dealers said buying interest in treasury bills pushed up prices and drove yields down.

The treasury bill maturing on January 11 was traded on Friday at a yield of 5.80 percent against its last traded 6.64. The July 18 treasury bill yielded 9.70 percent against 9.86 while the August 29 bill shed 15 basis points to 9.85 percent.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
"Top-rated companies are trying to place three-month commercial paper at 12.0-12.25 percent," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But investors are looking at returns above 13 percent."
